To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PPC can improve the quality of life of children and adolescents with a life-limiting disease and their families, and it can help families to prepare for the death of a child.
palliative care in pediatrics focuses on quality of life, is initiated at different times during the disease trajectory, and can be differentiated from EoL care.

pediatric palliative care (1) is a multidimensional, comprehensive care that is provided to children and their families from the time of diagnosis until death, (2) is a team effort that includes physicians and nurses, but also other health care professionals such as social workers, chaplains, and pharmacists, as well as the child’s primary care team, and (3) aims to improve the child’s quality of life and to provide support and comfort for the child and the family.

the development of a new approach to palliative care for children and their families.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PPC is a medical and psychosocial approach to improve the quality of life of children and adolescents with serious diseases, and their families.
the provision of PPC for children and adolescents is a medical necessity.
PPC is an important part of care for children at risk of dying and should be available to all children and families in need.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PPC is a holistic approach for children and adolescents who have a life-limiting condition.
PPC is an interdisciplinary, comprehensive, and family-centered care approach for children and adolescents with serious and/or complex conditions, which focuses on quality of life.
PPC should be integrated into the care of children and adolescents at the end of life and should be provided in a timely fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PPC should be initiated early enough to support the child and family in living well with a life-limiting disease.
PPC is not only for the EOL, but that it should start early and be integrated into the child’s care from the onset of the disease.
the earlier in the disease trajectory PPC is introduced, the better the outcome for the child and his family.
